newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling seen testing support on mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling seen testing support on mark.

text.p: Sterling's post election shakeout is healthy and forms a base for another test of the upside and the likelihood of tighter monetary policy points to a firmer pound.

Sterling previous support/congestion level around 2.8060-80 will provide upside resistance this time and beyond that 2.8230 marks -- around sterling/mark's 4-1/2 year high -- is the next substantial resistance area.
Proceedings were somewhat overshadowed this morning when the U.K. Treasury announced that Wednesday's monthly monetary meeting had been brought forward to today.

Analysts said even though a near-term rate rise would help sterling higher, it has come up so far that a further correction down to support around round figure support at 2.7900 marks is very much on the cards.
"Sterling/mark should struggle to regain 2.8070-2.8170 and I'm favouring a test of 2.7865-50 in the near-term," said one technical analyst at a leading U.S. bank.
The 2.7865-50 level represents the late April congestion area.
Cable is also seen consolidating further and will see $1.6160 to $1.6100 again before bouncing, analysts said.
At 0800 GMT the pound was at 2.7978/88 marks after earlier slipping to a low of 2.7925 compared with Monday's 2.8010/20.
Cable was at $1.6181/91 against a low of $1.6170 and previous $1.6201/13.
The pound moved off its lows after the Treasury announced that the monetary meeting had been brought forward to today.
The new Chancellor Gordon Brown will make a statement after the meeting at 1000 GMT. Most in the market believe the meeting will result in a quarter point rise in six percent base lending rates.
Rates were last raised a quarter on October 30, 1996.
RSI - 14 day: Sterling/mark: 56 pct, sterling/dollar: 47 pct
